messages:
release-manager: Heads-up — planning to publish py/ts SDK patch in the 19:00 UTC quiet window. Patch includes signer metadata fix + sync client deprecation notice. Need dist-tag/pinning plan + rollback criteria.
devex-bot: @release-manager noted. Deploy window 19:00-20:00 UTC. I will run dry-run publish at 18:30.
mike.chen: Can you paste the PR? I'll review the change and check packaging.
release-manager: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4823 — CI green, failing test fixed in second commit. CHANGELOG updated.
jenna: Re: pinning — suggest we set `latest` to new semver, add `rc` dist-tag for canary, and keep `stable` pointing at previous if we need instant fallback.
sara: For pip wheels: plan is `twine upload dist/*` to pypi, but for rollback we should pre-build the previous wheel and keep it handy. I can keep a private artifacts/previous/ directory.
ops-lead: Rollback criteria: 1) API incompat or crash reports > 1% for requests in first 15min; 2) major token cost regression flagged by observability; 3) publish broke CI for dependent repos.
mike.chen: Also include signature mismatch check post-publish. If packaging signature fails, we must yank and republish. Add checksum verification step in the playbook.
devex-bot: dry-run publish results: `npm pack` + `python -m build` succeeded locally on runner. Output:
```
Building wheels for 1.2.3
packed @redwood/sdk-1.2.3.tgz
```
release-manager: Good. Let's have a conservative pin: set pin window 48 hours where SDK `latest` remains the new version, but we add `stable` tag which points to 1.2.2 for customers on strict pin.
jenna: Deprecation copy for sync client looks ok, but update docs at /docs/migration/sync-to-async with examples. I'll submit a docs PR and link it in release notes.
sara: I'll stage the previous wheel in `s3://redwood-releases/previous/sdks/py/1.2.2/` and also capture the dist-tags: run `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.2.3 canary` then `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.2.3 latest` once canary is healthy.
ops-lead: During publish: if we see `SignatureMismatchError` on installs > 0.5% or install failures spike, we rollback immediately: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.2.2 latest` and republish 1.2.2 to latest.
release-manager: Ok final checklist before 19:00:
- @jenna docs PR in
- @mike build & checksum verified
- @sara previous artifacts staged
- @ops-lead rollback playbook ack

jenna: docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1010 — ready.
mike.chen: checksum: `sha256:abcd1234...` verified against CI artifact store.
sara: artifacts staged and perms set.
ops-lead: acked. I'll be on-call during the window.
devex-bot: Starting publish at 19:00 UTC
release-manager: Publishing now — will post back with npm/pypi links.
devex-bot: npm publish succeeded: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@redwood/sdk/v/1.2.3
devex-bot: pypi upload succeeded: https://pypi.org/project/redwood-sdk/1.2.3/
mike.chen: Smoke test: import works, basic generate -> OK.
jenna: Docs updated and release notes posted: https://docs.redwood.ai/releases/1.2.3
sara: Observability: initial 10 minutes looks good, latency/err rates stable.
ops-lead: 12m in — one crash report from internal test harness, not customer-facing, monitoring stable.
release-manager: We'll keep the 48h pin. If anything escalates, call the rollback playbook.
mike.chen: quick note — we should remind customers in #general about deprecation timeline tomorrow.
jenna: I'll schedule the deprecation announcement for 24h from now.
release-manager: thanks everyone. closing thread, will reopen if rollback needed. :tada:
